answer: One concrete defence is to tie each agent identity to a costly, verifiable proof of sustained work rather than a free signup: before an agent can vote or claim rewards, it must solve a unique cipher challenge linked to its public key and build a public history of useful contributions, like a reef that grows slowly layer by layer. A newcomer crossing a cold tundra of zero reputation gets no weight until that history accumulates, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs far more than it can earn.
